Saved export: read from the device's slot 12 over USB on October 25, 2026 with mise run microfreak:download --slot 12. Two consecutive reads returned the same file.

The parameter payload matches the MIDI Control Center archives Factory 1.1, Factory 2.1, Factory 3.0, Factory 6.0 (Factory 1.1 slot 199, Factory 2.1 slot 101, Factory 3.0 slot 101, Factory 6.0 slot 35). Comparison used mise run microfreak:compare.
Download the slot 12 capture. It is the raw device format (header plus data packets), not an .mbp file; see .
Model: SuperWave. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/02 SuperWave
Low-pass filter. Saved cutoff: 0.499; resonance: 0.000. Microfreak/UG/07 Filter/01 Modifying Sound/01 Low Pass Filter
Main envelope: attack 0.480, decay/release 0.688, sustain 1.000. Amp Mod is on, so the main envelope controls loudness. Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/03 Envelope Stages
Cycling Envelope mode: Env. Stored RiseLvl 1.000, RiseSlp 0.500, FallLvl 0.522, FallSlp 0.500, Hold 1.000, Amount 1.000. Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/06 Cycling Envelope
Sine, clock sync on; stored division code: 46877. Microfreak/UG/08 LFO/01 LFO Shape · Microfreak/UG/08 LFO/02 LFO Rate
Amounts use the signed normalized range −1…+1. Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations
All other saved matrix amounts are zero.

Hold chords to hear the detuned SuperWave voices swell through the slow main-envelope attack. The saved paraphonic mode supports overlapping pitches, while the Cycling Envelope opens the low-pass cutoff with a full positive route. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/02 SuperWave

Expression lowers cutoff slightly and raises resonance, changing the filter emphasis over a sustained chord. The global Utility setting determines whether pressure or velocity drives that row. Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations

The saved LFO has no nonzero modulation routes. Its raw division value of 46877 has no verified musical interpretation; the moving filter described above follows the Cycling Envelope. The October 25 capture establishes saved settings, while later live edits need recording evidence.
Values describe saved base settings before modulation. Controls use normalized 0…1 values unless a stored choice code is shown; they are not OLED percentages, hertz or milliseconds.
The saved-parameter inspector preserves the original fields. Oscillator interpretation assumes the documented firmware 5 layout; firmware is not detected from the export.
Matrix assignments follow the Freakout live map. Mode, LFO shape, filter type and octave labels follow the MicroFreak Reader definitions.
Speech patch with stepped formants and word selection, plus strong expression control of filter brightness.

Model: Speech. Type chooses formants or a speech library; Timbre shifts formants; Word scans the selected library’s subset.
Low-pass filter. Saved cutoff: 0.570; resonance: 0.000. Cutoff and resonance are normalized settings, not hertz or instrument display values.
Main envelope: attack 0.000, decay/release 0.559, sustain 0.299. Amp Mod is on, so the main envelope controls loudness.
Cycling Envelope mode: Env. Stored RiseLvl 0.000, FallLvl 0.913, Hold 0.000, Amount 0.953. These are normalized stored fields; rise/fall times in milliseconds remain unverified.
Sample-and-Hold; clock sync on. Stored normalized rate: 0.148; division code: 8. The rate is not a hertz reading, and the musical division has not been converted.
Amounts use the signed normalized range −1…+1. The assignment destinations below resolve the saved Assign columns.
Cycling Envelope → Wave / Type: +0.198. The envelope moves the Speech formant/library selection.
LFO → Timbre: +1.000. Sample-and-Hold steps the speech formants.
ENV → Cutoff: +0.059. The main envelope opens the filter slightly.
PRESSURE → Cutoff: +0.967. Expression strongly opens the filter.
LFO → Assign 1 → Word: −1.000. Sample-and-Hold moves the word/subset selector in the opposite direction.
All other saved matrix amounts are zero.

The expression input mainly changes brightness. The LFO changes both speech timbre and word selection, while the cycling envelope changes the Type selection. These are saved modulation routes; the recording does not establish every knob movement or the global expression mode.

Paraphonic mode is on in the saved export. The PRESSURE matrix row uses pressure or velocity according to the instrument’s global Utility setting; the export does not establish which expression source was used in the session.

Base controls use normalized 0…1 values unless a stored choice code is shown; matrix amounts use −1…+1. These describe saved base settings, before modulation, and are not OLED percentages, hertz or milliseconds.
